cls: Anti-EGFR recombinant human IgG2 monoclonal antibody (antineoplastic)
pharm: Binds the epidermal growth factor receptor (EGFR), blocking ligand binding and downstream signaling, inhibiting tumor cell growth, survival, and angiogenesis.
quick: 6 mg/kg IV infusion over 60-90 minutes every 14 days
Can cause fetal harm; avoid - effective contraception required
Do not breastfeed during and for 2 months after the last dose
No specific adjustment studied; not renally cleared
Skin/dermatologic toxicity, serum electrolytes (magnesium, calcium, potassium), infusion reactions, RAS status
summary: Panitumumab is a fully human anti-EGFR IgG2 monoclonal antibody used to treat wild-type RAS (KRAS and NRAS) metastatic colorectal cancer, alone or with FOLFOX/FOLFIRI chemotherapy. It is NOT effective and should NOT be used in patients with RAS-mutant tumors. The dominant toxicities are dermatologic (acneiform rash, skin toxicity, paronychia, photosensitivity) and electrolyte disturbances, especially hypomagnesemia (also hypocalcemia and hypokalemia). It carries a boxed warning for dermatologic toxicity. Infusion reactions and, rarely, severe diarrhea (especially with chemotherapy) and pulmonary fibrosis can occur.
indications: Wild-type RAS (KRAS and NRAS) metastatic colorectal cancer as first-line therapy in combination with FOLFOX
Wild-type RAS metastatic colorectal cancer as monotherapy after disease progression on fluoropyrimidine-, oxaliplatin-, and irinotecan-containing chemotherapy

dosage.d: 6 mg/kg administered as an intravenous infusion over 60 minutes every 14 days
dosage.n: Infuse over 90 minutes if dose >1000 mg

dosage.d: Reduce infusion rate by 50% for the duration of that infusion
Withhold; if improves to <=grade 2 within 1 month, resume at 50% of original dose and escalate as tolerated
dosage.n: Discontinue if not recovering or recurrent severe toxicity

admin: Administer only after confirming wild-type RAS (KRAS and NRAS) status; do not use in RAS-mutant tumors
Give as an intravenous infusion via infusion pump with a low-protein-binding 0.2 or 0.22 micron in-line filter
Do not administer as IV push or bolus; dilute in 0.9% sodium chloride
Infuse over 60 minutes (90 minutes if dose exceeds 1000 mg); reduce rate by 50% for mild/moderate infusion reactions
Do not mix with other medications or dextrose solutions; flush line with saline before and after
moa: Panitumumab is a recombinant fully human monoclonal IgG2 antibody that binds specifically to the extracellular domain of the human epidermal growth factor receptor (EGFR/HER1). By competitively preventing binding of natural ligands (EGF and TGF-alpha), it blocks receptor autophosphorylation and downstream RAS-RAF-MAPK and PI3K-AKT signaling. This inhibits cell proliferation, induces apoptosis, and decreases production of pro-angiogenic factors and matrix metalloproteinases. Activating mutations in RAS (KRAS/NRAS) constitutively activate downstream signaling independent of EGFR, rendering anti-EGFR therapy ineffective in RAS-mutant tumors.

absolute: RAS-mutant (KRAS or NRAS) metastatic colorectal cancer or unknown RAS status (lack of efficacy/potential harm)
relative: History of severe infusion reaction to panitumumab
Pre-existing interstitial lung disease / pulmonary fibrosis
monitor: Serum magnesium, calcium, and potassium during and for 8 weeks after therapy

preg: Based on its mechanism and animal data, panitumumab can cause fetal harm (including embryolethality and abortion). Advise females of reproductive potential to use effective contraception during treatment and for 2 months after the last dose, and inform of the risk to the fetus.
lact: Because of the potential for serious adverse reactions in the breastfed infant, advise women not to breastfeed during treatment with panitumumab and for 2 months after the final dose.
renal: No formal renal impairment studies have been conducted. As a monoclonal antibody it is not eliminated by the kidneys, so renal impairment is not expected to require dose adjustment.
hepatic: No formal hepatic impairment studies have been conducted. Hepatic metabolism is not a major clearance route for monoclonal antibodies; no specific dose adjustment is recommended.

major: Oxaliplatin-based chemotherapy in RAS-mutant or unknown-RAS tumors - decreased survival; do not combine
Concurrent bevacizumab plus chemotherapy - increased toxicity and shorter survival; avoid
moderate: Irinotecan/fluoropyrimidine regimens - additive diarrhea and dermatologic toxicity
minor: No significant cytochrome P450-based interactions (it is a protein antibody)
interactions.diagnostics: Requires RAS (KRAS/NRAS) mutation testing of the tumor before use; monitor serum electrolytes.

common: Erythema, skin exfoliation, dry skin, pruritus
serious: Severe dermatologic toxicity (boxed warning) including skin infection, sepsis, abscess
emergency: Acute interstitial lung disease / respiratory failure

monitoring: Skin and soft-tissue toxicity throughout therapy
Serum magnesium, calcium, and potassium periodically during and for 8 weeks after treatment
counsel: This medicine is only effective if your tumor does not have a RAS (KRAS/NRAS) mutation
Expect skin rash, dryness, and nail changes; limit sun exposure, use sunscreen and moisturizers, and report severe or infected rash
You will have blood tests to check magnesium and other minerals - report muscle cramps, weakness, or irregular heartbeat
Tell staff immediately during the infusion if you feel chills, fever, breathlessness, or chest tightness
Use effective contraception during and for 2 months after treatment, and do not breastfeed during this time
pk: Pharmacologic EGFR blockade begins with infusion; clinical response over weeks
End of infusion (Cmax); steady state by the third dose
Refrigerate vials at 2-8 C; protect from light; do not freeze or shake
pearls: Use ONLY in wild-type RAS (KRAS and NRAS) tumors - RAS mutation predicts lack of benefit and possible harm
Boxed warning: dermatologic toxicity - acneiform rash severity often correlates with response
Hypomagnesemia is characteristic of anti-EGFR antibodies; monitor and replace magnesium aggressively
Fully human IgG2 (vs chimeric cetuximab) - lower rate of hypersensitivity/infusion reactions but reactions still occur
Avoid combining with bevacizumab-containing chemotherapy due to increased toxicity and worse outcomes
missed: Panitumumab is given by a healthcare professional on a set schedule (every 14 days). If you miss a scheduled appointment, contact your oncology team promptly to reschedule the infusion.
overdose: Doses up to about twice the recommended dose (12 mg/kg) have been studied; expected effects are exaggerated dermatologic toxicity and electrolyte disturbances. There is no specific antidote; manage with supportive care, electrolyte replacement, and skin care.
